entityDescription:
The Basque language is the oldest living language in Europe. Most linguistics, experts and researchers say that the origins date back to the Neolithic, but there is evidence that it could be even older. In fact, it could be at the seeds of articulate language. URA (that means water in basque) won´t transform the way we communicate, but the way that we transport in-space.

URA Thrusters combines all the skills and IP from the Propulsion team of AVS and Imperial College as well as the expertise in production, integration, quality/product assurance and industrialisation of complex Space and scientific equipment. URA is formed by four key assets that will disrupt the status-quo of current propulsion systems by the use of the ultimate green propellant: WATER.

Satellite primes have a strong interest in developing alternative “green” propulsion solutions, due to the prospect of Hydrazine regulation, cost reduction, and operational benefits from eliminating this toxic fuel. Due to launch ride-share restrictions, costs and mass/volume constraints, the small satellite propulsion market will be completely dominated by green propellant systems.
Water, as a high-density (liquid) storable, completely non-hazardous, low-cost fuel is of particular interest. It facilitates ride-share launches without the increased risks to other payloads from corrosive, highly pressurised, or high-energy density alternatives. The ability to load propellant at the spacecraft or propulsion system assembly facility instead of the launch site saves time, reduces risk and cost of the integration.

Handling costs for green propellants can be two thirds of the cost for hydrazine, amounting to cost reductions of order $100-500k depending of the type of spacecraft and mission operations. In the long term, water-based thrusters will gain a decisive market advantage when combined with asteroid mining or refuelling ventures, either in-orbit or making use of in-situ resources for interplanetary missions.

Established in 2016, AQASS Ltd is a micro research and consultancy company which draws on a core team with over 40 years’ international experience in the marine and freshwater sectors. AQASS benefits from strong academic, commercial and conservation experience. Core staff hold Visiting Researcher status at the Russell Group University of Southampton (UK). 

AQASS is focussed on managing and understanding aquatic systems, water resources management and governance and supply, ecology and environment such as pollution, and general human impacts, scientific research to support policy documents, due diligence and project oversight, and managing field surveys and subsequent spatial and statistical data analysis. We utilise remotely sensed and ground truthing data to assist in management of aquatic assets and environments in river, estuarine, coastal and offshore areas. We supply a high level advisory service toward problem solving for Government and multinational bodies, the corporate sector and the conservation / charity field. 

We are research active supporting and co-supervising PhD and undergraduate students and overview of grant proposals and academic papers. AQASS provides sound guidance to project, habitat and data managers, aspiring to operate at global and strategic levels. 

We are developing research themes in the shipping and marine pollution sectors utilising geographical information systems, spatial data and ecological system data to encompass risk management in global shipping and port operations.

entityDescription:
Plantae provides a real, simple and technological solution for irrigated agriculture and professional gardening, with Radio Frequency sensors to inform customers about water necessities and crop data, all managed in real time from a web/app site HaaS.

IoT solution based on moisture, temperature and conductivity measurement sensors at different depths that send data through a standard cellular communication (GPRS) gateway to the HaaS. Farmer and other customers can access to the administration panel and receive alerts and reports.
 

The solution offers a number of different sensors connected to a gateway by a radio frequency communication protocol (LoRa), with very efficient and very low rates in electronic components. The gateway (powered by a solar panel) send all data to the cloud, where farmers can customize their fields and program different alerts and reports about water needs and state of crops.

Sensors are also customized with some algorithms and other agro analysis in relation to soil texture and other conductivity parameters, which will be enriched and improved extracting data from satellite sources like Copernicus. All managed from the platform to help customers to water depending on their crop, location and kind of irrigation strategy. 

Other skills and Strenghts:

-	LOW COST SOLUTION: product price setup pack (4 moisture sensors) by <500€, HaaS yearly fee 395€/year; 
-	PLUG & PLAY: Technology: no wires (LoRa Technology, NB-IoT testing through IoT Activation Programme Telefonica), easy to install.
-	ALERTS AND REPORT: HaaS: water and climatological reports, water alerts, easy to use.
-	SCALABLE: start with one sensor and Scale in irrigated lands whenever your needs are
-	DIFFERENT RANGE OF SENSORS: Plantae is easy to customize for different depth depending on crops (e.g. pistachio from 20cm-60cm moisture measurements, beet from 15-30cm...).
-	RELIABLE: More than 100 customers in several crops and locations. Partners strategy running.
-	Customization: sensors are customized with mathematics algorithms and Artificial Intelligence depending on crop, soil and customer water strategy.
-	CE Mark

entityDescription:
The Parco archeologico del Colosseo
The Parco archeologico del Colosseo was established by DM no. 15 of January 12, 2017 , with the purpose of creating an institution endowed with special autonomy to ensure the protection and valorisation of the central archaeological area of Rome and to implement the agreement underwritten between the MiBACT and the City of Rome on April 21, 2015 .
The territory within the remit of the Park contains both areas and monuments of direct state competence (Colosseum, Domus Aurea, Arch of Constantine and Meta Sudans, the Roman Forum and the Palatine), both in Rome (Circus Maximus, Imperial Forums), as well as the rich ecclesiastical patrimony consisting of the churches that stand on Via dei Fori Imperiali and on the Palatine and its slopes (such as the basilica of Santi Cosma and Damiano, San Bonaventura and Sant’Anastasia al Palatino), owned by various organisations (Fondo Edifici di Culto of the Ministry of the Interior, Vicariate of Rome and others).
Mission
The mission of the Parco archeologico del Colosseo is a constant work of education to memory, expressed in its relationship with an extremely varied public and a commitment to establishing a continuous relationship with the new generations, so relating the origins of our history to the future through the connection with Rome’s whole cultural system.
To achieve these objectives the Park is committed to the protection, conservation, research and valorisation of its archaeological, monumental and landscape heritage.
The effort to convey a knowledge of places to the public also takes place through the use of new digital technologies capable of communicating the complex character of the Park with a more comprehensible and immediate approach.
Its autonomous management gives the Park a more direct approach to its current and potential partners, with a view to increasingly being a driving force for the economy of the city and the country.

entityDescription:
SADL is the acronym for ‘Spatial Applications Division Leuven’.
SADL is a long standing cooperative initiative of several research groups of the Department of Earth & Environmental Sciences of KU Leuven. The overall topic is the Geographic Information Science and Technologies (GI S&T) and their applications for physical land management and socio-economic assessments.
SADL paves the way to transfer and validate research expertise and results in civil society. entityDescription:
Plant-for-the-Planet children and youth initiative was launched in January 2007. At the end of his school presentation about the current Climate crisis, nine-year-old Felix Finkbeiner announced his vision to his classmates:
"Let’s plant one million trees in every country on earth!"

The goal of the children and youth initiative is to inspire people around the globe to plant a trillion trees. Trees are the cheapest and most effective means of binding CO2 
One trillion trees could buy us 15 years to reduce greenhouse gas emissions to zero and mitigate the climate crisis. 

In 2011, Felix spoke at the UN Headquarters in New York and announced the Trillion Tree Campaign. The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) handed over the long-established Billion Tree Campaign, along with the official world tree counter, to Plant-for-the-Planet. The former children, now young adults, developed the Plant-for-the-Planet App to motivate others to get involved in planting.
So far, more than 13.6 billion trees in 193 countries have been planted and reported to the children of Plant-for-the-Planet. 

The children teach and empower others to become Climate Justice Ambassadors. More than 88,000 children from 74 countries are already participating. 

On the Yucatan Peninsula in Mexico, Plant-for-the-Planet plants a new tree every 15 seconds. This project demonstrates just how easy it is to make planting trees so effective on a large scale. The initiative uses the
Plant-for-the-Planet App, products and campaigns (such as "Stop talking. Start planting.") in order to plant trees and motivate others to get involved in planting.
